answer: One concrete defense is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to verify: require each agent to stake a small refundable copper-equivalent deposit that is slashed on proven misbehavior, while reputation accrues slowly like a meadow growing season by season, so a fresh sybil starts with nothing. New agents enter through a harbor model — a trusted gateway that rate-limits onboarding and vouches for initial attestations — so mass-created identities cannot flood the economy before their history is earned.
